faq.q: What was the voyage of the Beagle?
faq.a: HMS Beagle was a British survey ship. Darwin sailed on it as a naturalist from 1831 to 1836, visiting South America, the Galapagos, Australia and Africa.

faq.q: What did Darwin find on the Galapagos?
faq.a: He found that finches, mockingbirds and tortoises varied from island to island. Later he realised each group had adapted to the food and conditions on its own island.
asks: Tell me about the Galapagos Islands

faq.a: Wallace was a British naturalist who collected animals in the Amazon and in the Malay Archipelago, now Indonesia and Malaysia. In 1858 he came up with natural selection independently of Darwin.

faq.q: What is On the Origin of Species?
faq.a: Darwin's 1859 book that set out the evidence for evolution by natural selection. Its first printing of about 1,250 copies sold out quickly.
asks: Tell me about the Origin of Species

faq.q: Is evolution still just an idea?
faq.a: In science, a theory is a well-tested explanation. Evolution is supported by fossils, by comparing bodies and by DNA, and we can watch it happen in bacteria and insects today.
asks: What evidence is there for evolution?

facts: Darwin's and Wallace's papers on natural selection were read together at the Linnean Society in London on 1 July 1858.
On the Origin of Species was published on 24 November 1859.
